name: PLLA / Sculptra perioral
lead: PLLA / Sculptra perioral refers to the use of poly-L-lactic acid, the active ingredient in the injectable product Sculptra, in the area around the mouth to stimulate collagen and soften wrinkles or restore volume. It is classed as a collagen stimulator rather than an immediate volumising filler.[1]

Poly-L-lactic acid is a biodegradable material. Reference descriptions say it provokes a foreign-body reaction in which macrophages release signalling molecules such as TGF-beta, prompting fibroblasts to produce collagen, and that it has been used in facial volume restoration, notably for HIV-associated lipodystrophy.[1] Evidence specific to the perioral region in the sources reviewed is limited to a registered trial still recruiting.
infobox: Injection; topical with microneedling under study
About 6 months to 2 years (reference estimate for PLA implants)

paras: Sculptra is described as an injectable filler used to add facial volume.[1] In perioral treatment it is used by clinicians with the aim of improving fine lines and loss of support around the mouth through gradual collagen production, rather than adding immediate lip volume.
The same material is used for HIV-associated facial lipodystrophy.[1]

Reference sources describe a foreign-body reaction in which macrophages release mediators including TGF-beta that signal fibroblasts to make collagen, which underlies the dermatological applications.[1]
Polylactic acid implants break down over roughly six months to two years into lactic acid, which the reference article describes as innocuous.[1]

One registered trial, NCT07225348, is a phase 4 study of 26 participants began in November 2025 and recruiting at last listing, testing topical poly-L-lactic acid combined with a microneedling device for perioral wrinkles.[2] No results were available in the sources reviewed, so no conclusion about effectiveness for the perioral area can be drawn from them.

timeline.event: Phase 4 trial of topical PLLA with microneedling for perioral wrinkles begins recruiting.[2]

refs.title: Treatment of Perioral Wrinkles Using Topical Poly-L-lactic Acid and Microneedling Device

card.summary: A collagen-stimulating injectable used around the mouth; perioral evidence in the sources reviewed is one ongoing trial.
card.note: Clinician-administered; no perioral trial results available in sources reviewed.

quick.overview:
PLLA is the active ingredient in Sculptra, an injectable that stimulates the skin to make collagen. People use it around the mouth to soften wrinkles and restore support gradually.

A phase 4 trial of topical PLLA with microneedling for perioral wrinkles is recruiting; no results were found.
quick.mechanism: The material triggers a foreign-body reaction in which macrophages release signals such as TGF-beta, prompting fibroblasts to produce collagen. It degrades over about six months to two years into lactic acid.
quick.risks: Nodules are a recognised concern with injectable collagen stimulators generally, though the sources reviewed did not detail rates. It is a clinician-administered product; rules vary by country.
